verdict: Datadog grew revenue 35% to $1.20B as big customers expanded their usage, and GAAP profit more than tripled to $118M — though once stock pay is added back, operating profit was $334M, which shows how much of the pay bill is shares.

segments.name: Platform subscriptions
segments.note: One integrated platform — monitoring, security and AI observability, priced per host and per feature. Datadog reports a single revenue stream.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the platform and its AI features — by far the biggest running cost.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to engineering and security teams at large companies.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

takeaways.title: Growth re-accelerated
takeaways.text: Revenue growth hit 35%, and customers spending $100k+ a year rose 20% to about 4,860 — big companies keep putting more of their systems on Datadog.

takeaways.title: A cash machine underneath
takeaways.text: Free cash flow was $251M in one quarter — 21 cents per revenue dollar — because subscriptions are paid upfront and stock pay costs no cash.

takeaways.title: Two margins, one gap
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin was 6%; non-GAAP was 28%. Almost the entire gap is stock-based compensation — pay delivered in shares rather than cash.

otherDetail: Other income of $50M, net — mostly interest earned on Datadog's $5.2B of cash and investments.
follow100Note: Rows add up with a small rounding difference.
